about: Docs/Design/84 §15.3: the talk scorecard (tools/talk_score.py), from talk_sim transcripts. T2 was frozen again in Phase 1 (2026-11-16) from its runs (artifacts/talk/runs/p1): Data/Talk/truth.json's rules replaced P0's provisional lexicon, so its old value no longer measured the same thing; every other metric is Phase 0's.

R4.name: distinctive line heard again within 10 h, per 100 h

R7.name: distinct reply entries per 1,000 reply beats

R8.name: habit saturation (% of a speaker's lines, mean)

C2.name: replies at the best fit available (%)

C3.name: endings by a farewell or a marked break (%)

C6.name: same entry or question twice in a conversation, per 1,000

T3.name: self-reference errors (own name, the listener in the third person, unbacked eyewitness words), per 1,000 lines

T4.name: identity drift: a stance changed with no event or concede, or answered against one's own, per 1,000 stance lines

T5.name: telling what the listener already believes, with no 'known' answer (%)

D1.name: lines with a dialect's words (%): accent none

D2.name: another dialect's words in a speaker's line

D3.name: dialect guessed from 20 lines (%): light and broad

U1.name: a resident's lines from their own words (%)

K3.name: same news told twice to the same resident

W3.name: a resident answers chat with the option off

X1.name: lexical cohesion: replies sharing a content word with the line before (%)
X1.target: diagnostic (not in §15.3): shows the control is discriminating

D1L.name: lines with a dialect's words (%): light speakers

D1B.name: lines with a dialect's words (%): broad speakers

C1Q.name: questions answered: the '?' heuristic (%)
C1Q.target: diagnostic (C1 until Phase 3; doesn't separate from the control)

T6.name: 'they' said of one known wolf named in the line, per 1,000 lines

D1A.name: lines said a step broader or plainer than the speaker's own accent (%)

control.how: talk_sim --ablate shuffle: lines after the first replaced by lines said at the same side of other conversations on the same topic, by a speaker of the same dialect where possible (§15.5)

refrozen.why: Slice 1's review (doc 84 §26): T1 locked at the 0 Phase 1 reached; T3 now counts the listener named in the third person and unbacked eyewitness words too, C3 only farewells and marked breaks, D1 gates accent none (light and broad are D1L and D1B, soft): measured again with their new definitions on the review's own run

Doc 84, Phase 2: new rows, first measured here (P2's card, artifacts/talk/runs/p2; its transcripts are Slice 1's word for word). C1M, owed answers answered by moves, replaces the '?' heuristic C1 from Phase 3 (§23); M1, lines carrying moves, is Phase 2's gate (transcripts carry moves). No existing row moved.

Phase 3 (doc 84 §28): definitions changed, measured again on Phase 2's own transcripts (artifacts/talk/runs/p2, rescored as p2r) so Phase 3 is compared like for like. C1 is now the owed answers by moves (Phase 2's C1M, the hard gate from Phase 3) and the '?' heuristic is C1Q; C2 is measured from Phase 3 (fit and best); C3 counts a last line that takes leave by its moves as well as by its words (with the dialects' farewells); C4 counts a grave-to-light clash by the lines' tones as well as the lexicon; R7 and X1 leave the closing pairs out (formulaic by design, §8.4); a move of its own (farewell.return) is no longer counted as another's kind (farewell).

Phase 3 (doc 84 §28): measured again on Phase 2's own transcripts (p2r). D3 is no longer 0% for a profile that heard one dialect (it isn't judged there; before, its 0 was weighed by the profile's lines, so the card moved with how much L1 heard); R8 and D3 are counted metrics for the noise test (R8: habit lines over the lines of speakers with 20 or more; D3: speakers guessed right of those judged).

Phase 3 (doc 84 §28): a card's D3 is now the mean over the profiles that judged it (weighed by their lines), not over every profile's lines with the unjudged ones counting nothing; measured again on Phase 2's own transcripts (p2r).

Phase 4 (doc 84 §29) measures them first: T5, a claim told to one who held it before the talk began with no 'I'd heard' (talk_sim's to_knew); C8, a third who joined (§8.9); B1, the director's beat and look timings as the card's runs see them (soft here: B1's gate is Tests/talk_bench alone). From Phase 4's own card, artifacts/talk/runs/p4.

Phase 4 (doc 84 §29) measures them first: T5, a claim told to one who held it before the talk began with no 'I'd heard' (talk_sim's to_knew); C8, a third who joined (§8.9); B1, the director's beat and look timings as the card's runs see them (soft here: B1's gate is Tests/talk_bench alone). From Phase 4's own card, artifacts/talk/runs/p4.

Doc 84 Phase 5: K1 counts the topics Data/Talk/topics.json calls everyday (the director's everyday floor reads the same flags), so the player topic (a traveller standing near), life (the town's births and weddings), times and price_cause are no longer counted as everyday; measured again on Phase 4's transcripts (artifacts/talk/runs/p4r)

Doc 84 Phase 5's gate (K1 35%+, K2 25% or less, K3 = 0): the topic director in data (topics.json: novelty, saturation, the everyday floor, favourites, closeness, the told set) moved the talk from news to everyday life by design, and C5 and C9 are measured for the first time (the talk turns along the topic graph; callbacks on the talk ledger); taken from Phase 5's card (artifacts/talk/runs/p5)

Doc 84 Phase 6 (r3-talk-p6): its gate measures T4 (identity drift, first measured: no stance aired drifted on the same basis or was answered against the speaker's own side) and D1, now judged by the accent each line was spoken in (accommodation, §10.6: a step broader toward kin and friends of one's own speech, plainer toward a class above, a stranger from elsewhere, a hostile pair; plain speech unshifted); D1A (lines so shifted), T6 ('they' said of one known wolf) and O1 (opinions given per 10 talks) are new rows.
